THE WORK OUTLINED HEREIN PROVIDES A HOLISTIC VIEW OF THE DEFENSE MOBILITY SYSTEM -
PHASE 1 SCOPE. THE WORK TO SUPPORT THE DELIVERABLES OF THIS PROJECT WILL BE CONDUCTED
BY A TEAM MADE UP OF THE FOLLOWING ORGANIZATIONS:
MICHIGAN TECHNOLOGICAL UNIVERSITY (MTU) KEWEENAW RESEARCH CENTER
MSC SOFTWARE CORPORATION (MSC)
HEXAGON US FEDERAL LUCIAD
RAMDO SOLUTIONS (RAMDO)
MTU WILL BE THE PRIME CONTRACTOR TO THE US GOVERNMENT WITH MSC ACTING AS A
SUBCONTRACTOR TO MTU. BOTH HEXAGON US FEDERAL AND RAMDO SOLUTIONS WILL BE
SUBCONTRACTORS OF MSC THROUGHOUT THIS PROJECT, WHEREIN MSC WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR
THE DELIVERABLES AND FINANCIAL OBLIGATIONS FOR THESE COMPANIES.
PROJECT WORK RESPONSIBILITIES FOR EACH TASK OR SUB-TASK HAVE BEEN IDENTIFIED IN THE
SCOPE BELOW. THE TIMELINE PRESENTED REPRESENTS: 1) A PRELIMINARY ESTIMATE; 2) THE
TIMELINE FOR THE ENTIRE PROJECT NOT JUST THE MSC PORTIONS. ALTERNATIVELY, THE COST
PRESENTED REPRESENTS THE COST FOR THE WORK TO BE PERFORMED BY MSC AND ITS
SUBCONTRACTORS. IT IS UNDERSTOOD THAT MTU WILL MANAGE THE OVERALL BUDGET FOR THIS
PROJECT AND AS SUCH HAS MADE ARRANGEMENTS TO FUND ITS PORTION OF THE WORK AND
DELIVERABLES.UNDER THIS SOW, MSC, ALONG WITH THE OTHER TEAM MEMBERS, SHALL CREATE A
CUSTOMIZED AND EXPANDED VERSION OF NG-NRMM FOR USE WITH ONBOARD VEHICLE
SYSTEMS AND LATER WITH AUTONOMOUS VEHICLES (BEYOND PHASE 1). THIS SHALL INCLUDE
BUILDING UPON KNOWLEDGE GAINED FROM CONDUCTING THE NG-NRMM CDT BACK IN
SEPTEMBER 2018. MSC SHALL CONDUCT THE FOLLOWING BELOW:
A. DEVELOP A NEW LEVEL OF VEHICLE MOBILITY INTELLIGENCE AND CONTROL THROUGH DATA
COLLECTION, COMPLEX TERRAMECHANICS, ADVANCED VEHICLE SENSING AND SIMULATION,
AND TESTING IN REAL WORLD ENVIRONMENTS.
B. DEVELOP SIMULATION ENVIRONMENT FOR VEHICLES TO OPERATE ON MULTIPLE TERRAINS TO
INCLUDE VALIDATED SIMULATION RESULTS WITH PHYSICAL TESTING.
C. DEVELOP REAL-TIME RE-ROUTING CAPABILITY TO COMMUNICATE WITH OPERATORS, MISSION
COMMANDERS, AND EVENTUALLY AUTONOMOUS VEHICLE OPERATION SYSTEM.
D. DEVELOP DATABASE OF VEHICLE AND SOIL INTERACTION TO BE USED BY OPERATORS AND
MISSION PLANNERS.
ADDITIONALLY, MSC SHALL DELIVER IMPROVED INTELLIGENCE IN THREE AREAS AS DESCRIBED
BELOW:
A. VEHICLE INTELLIGENCE MODELING SPECIFIC VEHICLE PERFORMANCE ATTRIBUTES ON
VARIOUS TERRAINS AND UNDER VARIOUS CONDITIONS.B. ENVIRONMENTAL INTELLIGENCE SENSING AND MODELING THE IMMEDIATE
SURROUNDINGS OF THE VEHICLE TO MAKE INTELLIGENT DECISION ON DIRECTION AND
SPEED.
C. GLOBAL INTELLIGENCE MODELING DYNAMIC MISSION CONDITIONS AND OBJECTIVE TO
SUCCESSFULLY ARRIVE AS QUICKLY AS POSSIBLE AND WITHOUT DETECTION.
2.1 WORK TASKS
TO ACCOMPLISH THE OBJECTIVES OF THIS PROJECT THE WORK WILL BE EXECUTE VIA FOUR (4)
MAJOR AREAS OF INTEREST AS DETAILED BELOW.
2.1.1 TASK 1: TERRAMECHANICS STUDIES
MSC & MTU SHALL CHARACTERIZE NEW SOIL TYPES, UNDERSTAND THE EFFECTS OF MOISTURE
CONTENT, CONDUCT CORRELATION STUDY BETWEEN HIGH AND LOW FIDELITY MODELS, AND APPLY
MACHINE LEARNING TECHNIQUES TO MODELS FOR FASTER PROCESSING. FURTHERMORE, MSC &
MTU SHALL CONDUCT VEHICLE TESTING OF TIRE AND SOIL INTERACTION, CONDUCT NEW TIRE
CHARACTERIZATION, AND CONDUCT TIRE AND SOIL CORRELATION WORK IN ADAMS SOFTWARE.
A. TERRAMECHANICS SOIL STRENGTH STUDIES.
A. BEVAMETER TESTS FOR NEW SOILS AND MOISTURE CONTENT. (MTU)
B. DISCRETE ELEMENT MODELING (DEM) MODELING OF VARIOUS SOIL TYPES WITH
MOISTURE. (MSC)
C. CORRELATION STUDIES HIGH AND LOW FIDELITY DEM MODELING. (MSC)
D. APPLYING MACHINE LEARNING (ML) TO DEM MODELING RESULTS. (MSC)
B. TIRE AND SOIL INTERACTION.
A. VEHICLE AS A BEVAMETER TESTS (TIRE AND SOIL INTERACTION). (MTU)
B. TIRE AND SOIL CORRELATION STUDY (PARAMETER IDENTIFICATION). (MSC)
C. TIRE TESTING, CHARACTERIZATION AND MODELING. (MSC)

TASK 1A: ASSESS AND STABILIZE VEHICLE AND SOFTWARE
I.	REVIEW GFI / GFE
II.	DEVELOP A SYSTEM STABILIZATION APPROACH PLAN 
III.	EXECUTE SYSTEM STABILIZATION PLAN TO ELIMINATE ERRATIC ELECTRICAL CONNECTIVITY AND POWER LEAKAGE, ENSURE RELIABILITY OF SENSOR OUTPUT AND EFFECTORS RESPONSES
IV.	STABILIZE CONTROL ARCHITECTURE TO ENSURE RELIABILITY OF CONTROL SIGNALS 
V.	DEVELOP INITIAL TECHNICAL DATA PACKAGE (TDP) TO INCLUDE DRAWINGS, ELECTRICAL HARNESS DRAWINGS. DEVELOP INITIAL INTERFACE CONTROL DOCUMENT (ICD) TO INCLUDE MECHANICAL, ELECTRICAL, AND CONTROL INTERFACE DESCRIPTIONS, DRAWINGS, AND SPECIFICATIONS.

TASK 1B: BASELINE PHYSICAL CHARACTERIZATION TESTING 
I.	DEVELOP SYSTEM AND SUBSYSTEM TEST PLAN
II.	CONDUCT TEST
III.	DOCUMENT RESULTS

TASK 2A: CREATE VIRTUAL PROVING GROUNDS (VPG) 
I.	USE UPDATED VEHICLE MODELS (CONTROLS AND DYNAMIC) WITH CONTRACTOR TEST COURSE VIRTUAL MODELS (TOPOLOGIES AND GEOTECHNICAL) 
II.	CORRELATE VIRTUAL AND PHYSICAL RESPONSES OVER VARIOUS DISTURBANCES AND MANEUVERS
III.	PROVIDE VIRTUAL PROVING GROUND (VPG) SOFTWARE DOCUMENTATION

TASK 3A: DEVELOP MAPPING DATABASE APPROACH AND MODIFY EXISTING PAM CONTROL SOFTWARE
I.	ESTABLISH CONTROL FRAMEWORK TO INTEGRATE REMOTE SENSING AND MAP DATABASE 
II.	UTILIZE TERRAIN DATABASE INFORMATION 
III.	INTEGRATE HYPERSPECTRAL IMAGERY TRAFFICABILITY TOOL (HITT) 
IV.	IDENTIFY ADDITIONAL REQUIRED SENSORS AND EFFECTORS 
V.	DEVELOP SENSORS INTEGRATION; ON-BOARD AND REMOTE
VI.	DEVELOP MAPPING DATABASE APPROACH 
VII.	DOCUMENT FRAMEWORK WITH AN INTERFACE CONTROL DOCUMENT (ICD)

TASK 3B:  DEVELOP A CONCEPT OF OPERATIONS (CONOPS) FOR COORDINATING EFFECTOR ACTIONS 
I.	BASE ON THE NEGOTIATED TERRAIN USING REMOTE SENSING DATA RECEPTION ALONG WITH LEADER AND FOLLOWER DATA EXCHANGES. 

TASK 3C: TERRAIN CHARACTERIZATION USING REMOTE SENSING 
I.	SUPPORT DEVELOPMENT, TESTING, AND DEMONSTRATION OF TERRAIN CHARACTERIZATION USING REMOTE SENSING (UNMANNED AERIAL VEHICLE (UAV)) BY ASSISTING AND COORDINATE FLIGHT AUTHORIZATIONS AROUND THE CONTRACTOR TEST COURSE.

TASK 4A: PROJECT DOCUMENTATION AND PRESENTATION OF RESULTS

HOWEVER, UNIQUE DESIGN AND ANALYSIS CHALLENGES EXIST FOR WIRELESS NETWORKS OF MOBILE AGENTS, AND THESE CHALLENGES ARE AMPLIFIED IN ADVERSARIAL CONDITIONS. IN RT3, WE FOCUS ON DESIGN AND ANALYSIS CHALLENGES FOR BOTH CONTROLLING AGENTS WITHIN A NETWORK AND CONTROLLING AGENTS OVER A NETWORK. FOR CONTROLLING AGENTS WITHIN A NETWORK, THE POSSIBLE INTERACTIONS BETWEEN AGENTS CAN BE MODELED USING A GRAPH. WE WILL SIGNIFICANTLY IMPROVE UPON PREVIOUS WORK ON THIS AREA BY MORE FULLY CAPTURING THE STOCHASTIC NATURE OF INFORMATION EXCHANGES THROUGH TIME-VARYING AND RANDOM GRAPH MODELS, SUCH AS TEMPORAL NETWORKS. WE BUILD UPON THESE MODELS BY (I) DETERMINING CONDITIONS UNDER WHICH RANDOM COMMUNICATION GRAPHS ATTAIN REQUIRED CONNECTIVITY PROPERTIES AND (II) POSITIONING AGENTS TO ACHIEVE NETWORK OBJECTIVES, SUCH AS ACHIEVING SPECIFIED CONNECTIVITY PROPERTIES OR JAMMING ADVERSARIAL NETWORKS. EXTENT OF A ROBOTÃƑÂ¢Ã¢Â€ŠÂ¬Ã¢Â€ŽÂ¢S MORAL INFLUENCE NECESSARILY DEPENDS ON WHETHER A ROBOT CAN BE SAID TO HOLD THE
STATUS OF A MORAL AGENT, THAT IS, AN ACTOR THAT HAS CERTAIN GENERAL CAPACITIES AND ABILITY FOR ACTION UPON
ITS ENVIRONMENT, COUPLED WITH THE CAPACITY FOR MORALLY RELEVANT ACTION. ESTABLISHING WHEN, HOW, AND
WHY ROBOTS ARE MORAL AGENTS IS KEY FOR ADVANCING HUMAN-ROBOT INTERACTION (HRI), IN PART DUE TO THE
MULTI-FACETED, MULTI-DISCIPLINARY IMPLICATIONS OF SAID AGENCY. FOR INSTANCE, WHETHER OR NOT A ROBOT
IS CONSIDERED A MORAL AGENT HAS SIGNIFICANT IMPLICATIONS FOR HOW RESEARCHERS, DESIGNERS, AND USERS
CAN, SHOULD, AND DO MAKES SENSE OF ROBOTS AND WHETHER THEIR AGENCY IN TURN TRIGGERS OTHER SOCIAL
AND MORAL COGNITIVE AND BEHAVIORAL PROCESSES IN OTHERS. ROBOTIC MORAL AGENCY ALSO HAS SIGNIFICANT
IMPLICATIONS FOR HOW PEOPLE SHOULD AND DO HOLD ROBOTS MORALLY RESPONSIBLE, ASCRIBE BLAME TO
THEM, DEVELOP TRUST IN THEIR ACTIONS, AND DETERMINE WHEN THESE ROBOTS WIELD MORAL INFLUENCE.
THUS, BECAUSE OF THE CRITICAL SIGNIFICANCE OF ROBOTIC MORAL AGENCY, RESEARCHERS FROM SEVERAL DISCIPLINES HAVE STARTED TO INVESTIGATE HOW WE CAN DETERMINE WHETHER AND TO WHAT EXTENT ROBOTS CAN
BE DETERMINED TO BE MORAL AGENTS. FOR EXAMPLE, IN THE PSYCHOLOGY LITERATURE, RESEARCHERS HAVE
DEVELOPED MEASURES INTENDED TO CAPTURE HUMAN PERCEPTIONS OF MORAL AGENCY, THAT IS THE DEGREE TO
WHICH OBSERVERS PERCEIVE ROBOTS TO BE MORAL AGENTS. HOWEVER, THERE ARE SEVERAL PSYCHOLOGICAL AND
PHILOSOPHICAL CHALLENGES TO THE CONSTRUCTION OF THESE MEASURES, INCLUDING CONFLATING GOOD MORAL
COMPETENCE (E.G., OPERATING IN A WAY THAT IS MORALLY GOOD) WITH MORAL AGENCY, WHERE SIMPLY BEING
A MORAL ACTOR DOES NOT NECESSITATE THAT THE ACTOR IS A GOOD MORAL ACTOR.
FURTHER AND MORE FUNDAMENTALLY, THE COMMON APPROACH TAKEN IN THE EXISTING LITERATURE LIMITS
ROBOT MORAL AGENCY TO A PURELY PSYCHOLOGICAL CONSTRUCT RATHER THAN AN ONOTOLOGICAL STATE OF BEING. ALTHOUGH THIS DISTINCTION IS NUANCED, IT IS A CRITICAL ONE TO MAKE. FRAMING MORAL AGENCY AS
A PURELY PSYCHOLOGICAL CONSTRUCT WOULD IMPLY THAT HUMANS HAVE AN INTUITIVE UNDERSTANDING AND
MENTAL CONCEPTUALIZATION OF THE DEGREE TO WHICH A ROBOT OR OTHER AUTONOMOUS AGENT IS A MORAL
AGENT. CHANGES IN AND FEATURES OF ROBOT DESIGNS AND BEHAVIORS WOULD LIKELY INFLUENCE THE DEGREE
TO WHICH SUCH AGENCY IS ASCRIBED TO THE ROBOT FROM THE HUMAN MIND. AN ONTOLOGICAL FRAMING, ON
THE OTHER HAND, WOULD SUGGEST THAT (MOST) HUMANS DO NOT HAVE AN INTUITIVE UNDERSTANDING OF THE
PHILOSOPHICAL CONCEPT OF ROBOT MORAL AGENCY. TO ILLUSTRATE, ALTHOUGH ROBOT DESIGN INFLUENCES PERCEPTIONS OF THE CONSTITUENT PSYCHOLOGICAL CONSTRUCTS OF MORAL AGENCY, LIKE AUTONOMY AND ADAPTABILITY,
THESE WOULD NEED TO BE LOGICALLY COMBINED TO PRODUCE ARGUMENTS IN FAVOR FOR OR AGAINST ANY GIVEN
ROBOTÃƑÂ¢Ã¢Â€ŠÂ¬Ã¢Â€ŽÂ¢S ONTOLOGICAL STATUS AS A MORAL AGENT BY ANY GIVEN HUMAN. THAT IS TO SAY, (1) JUST BECAUSE
AN ARGUMENT FOR AGENCY DEPENDS ON HUMAN PERCEPTIONS OF THE BUILDING BLOCKS OF AGENCY, IT DOES
NOT GUARANTEE THAT HUMANS DIRECTLY PERCEIVE ROBOT MORAL AGENCY; AND (2) A QUANTIFICATION OF ROBOT
MORAL AGENCY REQUIRES SUBSTANTIALLY MORE CAREFUL ASSESSMENT OF THE ANTECEDENTS OF AGENCY, AS WELL
AS INFORMED APPROACHES FOR HOW EVIDENCE FOR THOSE ANTECEDENTS SHOULD BE LOGICALLY COMBINED TO
INFER WHETHER A ROBOT IS INDEED A MORAL AGENT.
TO ADDRESS THE CURRENT DEFICIENCY IN MORAL AGENCY CONCEPTUALIZATION AND MEASUREMENT, WE
PROPOSE TO DRAW UPON FIRST PRINCIPLES OF ROBOTIC MORAL AGENCY AS AN ONTOLOGICAL CATEGORY GROUNDED
IN PHILOSOPHY, AND SUPPORTED BY TECHNIQUES IN EXPERIMENTAL PSYCHOLOGY AND COGNITIVE SCIENCE.
WE WILL CREATE NEW METHODS FOR QUANTIFYING MORAL AGENCY IN WHICH RESEARCHERS (1) SEPARATELY
ASSESS THE CORE CONSTRUCTS OF CAPACITY FOR MORAL ACTION, PERCEIVED AUTONOMY, PERCEIVED INTERACTIVITY, AND PERCEIVED ADAPTABILITY, AND (2) LOGICALLY COMBINE THE OUTPUTS OF THOSE SCALES. WE WILL
WILL DRAW UPON EXPERIMENTAL PSYCH
